podcast.title: Polaris Music Prize Nomination (2006)
podcast.body: Metric was one of the bands nominated for the 2006 Polaris Music Prize, an award aimed at recognizing artistic merit over commercial success, though the prize was ultimately awarded to Final Fantasy. "The winning album was... By Final Fantasy... which won out over records by Broken Social Scene, The New Prenogpers, and Metric."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 4: (70-61)

podcast.title: Admiration for Mark Linkous
podcast.body: Metric was noted as an admirer of Mark Linkous, the songwriter and frontman for Sparklehorse, highlighting his respected status among his peers in the music industry. "He had fans of the flaming lips, and metric of the Silver Sun pickups, and Patty Smith and many others."

podcast.title: Beneficiary of Radio Star Maker
podcast.body: Metric's career was furthered by the funding available from the new Radio Star Maker program, introduced in 2000. This program, along with Factor, was instrumental in supporting emerging and established Canadian talent. "Soon this cash was instrumental in helping further the careers of metric, broken social scene, Alexis on fire, city and color, and many more."

podcast.title: Emily Haines's Entrepreneurial Ventures
podcast.body: Emily Haines has collaborated with a clothing company to create bespoke designs and has also launched her own fragrance called Siren. "She's worked with a clothing company to come up with bespoke designs, and she has her own fragrance called Siren."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Emily Haines's Philanthropic Work
podcast.body: Emily Haines is actively involved with "Fleet for Hear Me," an organization that supports children's music education programs in schools. She is also part of the Global Citizen Group, specifically its "She Decides" division, which focuses on women's issues. "She works with an organization called Fleet for Hear Me, which works with children's music education programs and schools. She's part of the Global Citizen Group, specifically with a woman's issues division called She Decides."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Founding Members' Independence
podcast.body: Emily Haines and James Shaw have consistently prioritized Metric's independence, choosing to operate outside the major label system and manage their affairs internally. This approach has proven highly successful and made them influential in the 21st century for maintaining creative and financial control. "They've insisted that Metric be as independent as possible, and they've done very well working outside the major label system and running things themselves."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Indie Rock Revival (2000s)
podcast.body: Metric is mentioned as one of the "fresh sounding bands" that emerged during the Indie Rock Revival in the early 2000s.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Dreampop - A History

podcast.title: Support for Other Female Artists
podcast.body: Emily Haines and James Shaw have extended their influence by supporting other female artists. In 2017, they collectively produced the debut album for the band Beaches, a collaboration that helped Beaches establish themselves as a significant force in Canadian rock. "I should point out that Emily and James Shaw have paid it forward when it comes to helping out other female artists. They collectively produce the debut album for Beaches in 2017, which helped them become a real force in Canadian rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Twilight Soundtracks Contribution
podcast.body: Metric contributed to the various *Twilight* soundtracks that accompanied the film series. These soundtracks featured a nice selection of tunes, mostly album cuts and outtakes, from a range of artists spanning different genres. "The Paramore, Lincoln Park, Collective Soul, Death Cab for Cutie, Tom York, the Killers, Editors, Metric, Block Keys, Dead Weather, Beck, Vampire Weekend, Florence in the Machine."

xref.title: Polaris Music Prize Win (2006)
xref.body: Final Fantasy, the project of Owen Pallett, received the Polaris Music Prize in its inaugural year, 2006, for the album "He Poos Clouds." This win generated controversy, as the prize aims to reward musical excellence without regard for genre or commercial success, leading to debate about its lasting impact compared to other nominated albums. "When the winning album was, he poos clouds. Yeah, great title. By Final Fantasy, the vehicle for one time arcade fire violinist Owen Palette, which won out over records by Broken Social Scene, The New Prenogpers, and Metric."

xref.title: Cultural References to His Death
xref.body: Bobby Fuller's mysterious death has been referenced in songs by various artists, including Lou Reed and Metric. The lasting impact of his music and the questions surrounding his passing resonate in popular culture. "Artists from Lou Reed to metric have reference Fuller in songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rock Stars Who Were Murdered

xref.title: Frontman's Reputation
xref.body: Sparklehorse was led by Mark Linkous, a highly respected songwriter from Richmond, Virginia. He garnered admiration from various notable artists and bands, including The Flaming Lips, Metric, The Silver Sun Pickups, and Patti Smith. "The group was Sparkle Horse. And they were led by a very well-regarded songwriter from Richmond, Virginia, named Mark Linkhouse."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Great Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of the 90s: Part 2

xref.title: Notable Guest Vocalists
xref.body: The band is known for featuring a variety of guest appearances on their tracks, including Emily Haines from Metric, Sarah McLachlan, and Matthew Sweet. "Delirium has been an ongoing project since 1987, using guest appearances, Emily Haynes of Metric, Sarah McLaughlin, and Matthew Sweet among them."
